items.title: Imitation
items.body:
A dark unfathomed tide
Of interminable pride--
A mystery, and a dream,
Should my early life seem;
items.quote:
I say that dream was fraught
With a wild and waking thought
Of beings that have been,
Which my spirit hath not seen,
items.author: Edgar Allan Poe

items.title: Remembrance
items.body:
'Tis done!--I saw it in my dreams:
No more with Hope the future beams;
  My days of happiness are few:
Chill'd by Misfortune's wintry blast,
items.author: George Gordon, Lord Byron

items.title: The Canterbury Tales. The Manciple's Tale.
items.body:
THE PROLOGUE.

WEET ye not where there stands a little town,
Which that y-called is Bob-up-and-down,
items.quote:
Under the Blee, in Canterbury way?
There gan our Hoste for to jape and play,
And saide, "Sirs, what? Dun is in the mire.
Is there no man, for prayer nor for hire,
items.author: Geoffrey Chaucer

items.title: The Daguerreotype
items.body:
This, then, is she,
My mother as she looked at seventeen,
When she first met my father. Young incredibly,
Younger than spring, without the faintest trace
items.quote:
Of disappointment, weariness, or tean
Upon the childlike earnestness and grace
Of the waiting face.
Those close-wound ropes of pearl
items.author: William Vaughn Moody

items.title: Winter Stores
items.body:
WE take from life one little share,
And say that this shall be
A space, redeemed from toil and care,
From tears and sadness free.
items.quote:
And, haply, Death unstrings his bow
And Sorrow stands apart,
And, for a little while, we know
items.author: Charlotte Bronte

items.title: Book II. Satire VI. the First Part Imitated in the Year 1714, by Dr
items.body:
SWIFT; THE LATTER PART ADDED AFTERWARDS.

I've often wish'd that I had clear,
For life, six hundred pounds a-year,
items.quote:
A handsome house to lodge a friend,
A river at my garden's end,
A terrace-walk, and half a rood
Of land, set out to plant a wood.
items.author: Alexander Pope

items.title: The Canterbury Tales. The Wife of Bath's Tale.
items.body:
THE PROLOGUE.

Experience, though none authority
Were in this world, is right enough for me
items.quote:
To speak of woe that is in marriage:
For, lordings, since I twelve year was of age,
(Thanked be God that is etern on live),
Husbands at the church door have I had five,
items.author: Geoffrey Chaucer

items.title: To Helen
items.body:
I saw thee once--once only--years ago:
I must not say _how_ many--but _not_ many.
It was a July midnight; and from out
A full-orbed moon, that, like thine own soul, soaring,
items.quote:
Sought a precipitate pathway up through heaven,
There fell a silvery-silken veil of light,
With quietude, and sultriness and slumber,
Upon the upturn'd faces of a thousand
items.author: Edgar Allan Poe
